en: Praise to Cakrasaṃvara (or Hymn to the Purification of Heruka).
Oṃ. Homage to the glorious Cakrasaṃvara!
I bow to the glorious Heruka, the great hero, the one who brings about the restraint of Cakrasaṃvara; the conqueror of Māra, the leader of the *ḍākinī* net. (1)
I pay homage to that Vajravārāhī, who conforms to great passion, and likewise to Ḍākinī, Lāmā, and the embodied Khaṇḍarohā. (2)
And the four vessels of nectar, filled with the thought of awakening (bodhicitta),
[he saw] at the summit of Pullīramalaya as the fierce Vajraḍākinī.
One should worship Jālandharaśikhā and Caṇḍākṣī, who has gone beyond all taint, in the head; and one should worship the goddess Prabhāvatī in both ears in the place called Oḍiyāna.
I bow to Arbudi on the backbone and to Mahānāsā;
I bow to Godāvarī in the left ear and to the auspicious Vīramatī in the right ear. || 5 ||
One should meditate on Rāmeśvarī between the eyebrows, the short-statured one of excellent complexion;
and on the goddess Śrīmallaṅkeśvarī, who resides in Devīkoṭṭa and possesses the splendor of Maitra.
In Mālava, at the region of the shoulders, I bow to Drumacchāyā;
in Kāmarūpa, at the two armpits, to the auspicious goddess Airāvatī.
One should worship the virtuous Śrī Mahābhairavā on the two breasts or in Oḍra;
and the beautiful Vāyuvegā in the navel or in the place called Triśakuṇi.
I bow to Surābhakṣī in Kośala or at the tip of the nose;
and to the eternal Śyāmādevī in the beautiful face of Kaliṅga.
One should worship Subhadrā, the most beautiful of women, at Lampāka in the region of the throat;
and Hayakarṇā, who is enchanting, at Kāñcī in the heart of the corpse.
In Himālaya, at Meḍhra, I bow to Khagānanā;
likewise, in Pretapurī, at Liṅga, I bow to Śasyanīśvarī in the north.
One should worship Gṛhadevatā in the region of the anus, the charming Khaṇḍarohā [in the genitals], Saurāṣṭrā on the pair of thighs, and Śauṇḍinī, the bestower of happiness, [on the knees]. 12.
In Suvarṇadvīpa, one should worship Cakravarmiṇī on the shank;
in the city, Suvīrā, the excellent Yoginī, on the place of the fingers.
One should meditate on the goddess Mahābalā stationed at the Sindhu river and on the two feet and the back,
and on Cakravartinī stationed at Maru and on the pair of big toes.
I bow to the Goddess Mahāvīryā at the two knees of Kulatā—
she who is preceded by Khaṇḍakapāla, Vīra, and others, and whose body is adorned with the remnants of her own wisdom.
Through my devotion, [I worship] the great heroines who reside in the wheels of body, speech, and mind:
Kākatuṇḍī, Ulūkāsyā, Śvānāsyā, and Śūkarānanā. (16)
I bow to these goddesses—Yamadāḍhī, Yamadūtī, Yamadaṃṣṭrī, and Yamāntikā—who are stationed in the cardinal and intermediate directions. (17)
Having praised Heruka, the supreme lord, the master of heroes and heroines, may whatever merit has been acquired by me through this [praise] belong to the circle of goddesses.
By that merit, may the world become Vajraḍāka, the teacher of all beings. || 18 ||
The praise of the Śrī Cakrasaṃvara is completed.
